clue.text: Gladiator scraps about cheers nearly ended

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for scraps surrounds the rest

parts.note: scraps as a verb means fights or spars
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is dropped from the word that follows

parts.note: ended means cut, as in cut short

explanation.surface: A gladiator brawls, the crowd applauds, and the bout is nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ended' is read as 'cut', as in cut short; 'scraps' is a verb meaning fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus was the Thracian gladiator who led the slave revolt against Rome, so he is a famous example.

clue.text: Ceremony broadcast without a crowd

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for broadcast goes round the rest

parts.note: broadcast means sent out on the airwaves
to crowd is to cram

explanation.surface: A ceremony is televised without any audience present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament is a Christian religious rite, such as baptism or communion, so it is a type of ceremony.

clue.text: Adult kiss on island revealing truth

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
X is the kiss at the end of a letter
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: An adult steals a kiss on an island holiday and something true comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is the Isle of Man, abbreviated IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as self-evidently true, a basic principle.

clue.text: Naked wearing rubbish silk

indicators.note: the rubbish is worn around the naked word, so it encloses it

parts.note: tat means cheap rubbishy goods
naked means bare

explanation.surface: Someone naked is dressed only in cheap silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabaret is an upholstery fabric of alternating satin and watered silk stripes.

clue.text: Be faithful embracing unrefined toadying

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the faithful word wraps the unrefined one

parts.note: to cling to someone is to stay loyal to them
raw means unrefined, as raw sugar

explanation.surface: A loyal follower hugs someone crude while sucking up to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Crawling means behaving obsequiously to win favour, the same as toadying or fawning.

clue.text: Part of church in deterioration's uplifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifted means the letters are read from bottom to top
in places the church inside the word for deterioration

parts.note: rot is decay; with the 's it becomes rots
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Part of the church building has risen up as it falls into decay.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is part of the fodder: deterioration's gives the plural-style form, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct section or division of something, so a portion.

clue.text: Struggle with belief

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: Someone is grappling with their faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is an opinion or conviction someone holds.

clue.text: What aroma nicely rising enshrouds lover

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
enshrouds says the phrase wraps the letters wanted, concealed inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pleasant scent rises and wraps around a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'enshrouds lover' as the definition, but 'enshrouds' is the signal that the letters are concealed in 'What aroma nicely'; 'lover' alone is the definition. 'rising' reads them upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover or sweetheart, from Italian.

clue.text: Makes water, obscuring pupils primarily

indicators.note: obscuring means hiding, so the urinating word covers the letter

parts.note: to make water is to urinate, which is wees

indicators.note: primarily means first, picking the opening letter of pupils

explanation.surface: Someone urinates, blinding schoolchildren.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes crying: tears are water that blur the eyes' pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeping produces tears that well over the eyes, so it makes water that obscures the pupils.

clue.text: Heavenly region around stellar twelve revolving

indicators.note: revolving turns the assembled letters right round

parts.note: C is short for circa, around
stellar means first-rate, A1, written here as AI
DOZ is the abbreviation for dozen

explanation.surface: A band of the sky turns around its twelve star signs.
explanation.walkthrough: Stellar means first-rate, A1, with the figure 1 standing for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac is the belt of sky through which the sun, moon and planets move, divided into twelve signs.

clue.text: Ascent of Conservative member

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is an upward movement or an uphill route.

clue.text: Branch or agency covering foreign city

indicators.note: the phrase covers the answer, holding its letters inside

parts.note: the letters run across the words

explanation.surface: A local office or agency handles business for an overseas city.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorage is the largest city in Alaska, in the United States.

clue.text: The main man, in the main

definitions.text: The main man, in the main

parts.words: The main man, in the main
parts.note: the main is old poetic language for the sea, so the top man at sea is a naval commander

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main man' reads as slang for the boss; 'the main' is the sea, so the chief in the navy is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the most senior rank of naval officer, commanding a fleet on the high seas.

clue.text: Unlucky over without taking duck

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the without word holds the duck

parts.note: minus means without
a duck is a score of nought, O

explanation.surface: A batsman out for nothing feels his over has gone badly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous means foreboding or ill-starred, suggesting bad luck to come.

clue.text: Going outside, catching cold, causing fever

indicators.note: catching means holding the cold inside

parts.note: exiting means going out
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Stepping out of doors, someone catches a chill and runs a temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing fever' looks medical, but it means stirring up excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exciting stirs up feverish enthusiasm or agitation.

clue.text: Japan maybe supporting auto plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath

parts.note: an auto is a car
Japan is an example of a nation

explanation.surface: Japan backing its motor industry by building a car factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory, but it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The carnation is a garden flower, a type of pink.

clue.text: Fancy clubs with dance party

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: Someone fancies going clubbing and on to a rave.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave something is to long for it, as to fancy it.

clue.text: Charming losing Democrat fit for office

indicators.note: losing means dropping the Democrat from the front

parts.note: delectable means delightful or charming

explanation.surface: A charismatic politician without the party label is still a good candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Electable means able to win an election, suitable to be voted into a post.

clue.text: Bare below? Possibly change material

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means the bare word goes under the other

parts.note: loose change is one possible form of cash
mere means bare, as in the bare minimum

explanation.surface: Someone half-dressed wonders about changing into better clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine soft wool from Kashmir goats, a luxury fabric.

clue.text: Abrupt end to Celt language

indicators.note: end to picks the final letter of Celt

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: A Celtic tongue ends sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief to the point of curtness.

clue.text: Clairvoyance with endless practice produces life

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a rite is a ritual practice

explanation.surface: Second sight plus constant training gives someone a new existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is liveliness of mind, spirit or vivacity, as life in a person.

clue.text: Cut charge on shoestring

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means attached after

parts.note: a shoestring is a shoelace
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Cutting costs by running a business on a shoestring budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on shoestring' suggests a tiny budget, but it is the shoelace.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or gash the flesh.

clue.text: One overcomes after firstly escaping bailiff

indicators.note: after places the victor word following the letter
firstly picks the first letter of escaping

parts.note: a victor is one who overcomes

explanation.surface: A prisoner flees and then gets the better of the bailiff.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor removes tenants from property, a job carried out by a bailiff.

clue.text: Symbol of French corruption

parts.note: de is French for of
vice is moral corruption

explanation.surface: An emblem of French decadence.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a device is an emblem or motto borne on a shield.

clue.text: Plod arrests nabbing one with ecstasy

indicators.note: nabbing means catching, so the trapping word holds the one

parts.note: traps means catches or arrests
I is the Roman numeral for one
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: The police arrest someone carrying ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Plod is British slang for the police, but here it is a verb meaning trudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or reluctantly, to trudge.

clue.text: Head in charge? It's debatable

definitions.note: a noun phrase sense: a subject that can be debated

parts.note: the top is the head of something

explanation.surface: Whether the boss is really running things is open to question.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject for discussion or argument.

clue.text: Look almost sweet after hard trim

indicators.note: after puts the look and sweet words following the hard letter

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
an air is a look or appearance

indicators.note: almost means losing the last letter

parts.note: cute means sweet

explanation.surface: A cute look after a severe trim at the barber's.
explanation.definitionFit: A trim at the barber's is a light haircut.

clue.text: Empty catacomb contains curious piece

indicators.note: contains means the outer letters hold the rest
empty means remove the middle, leaving the first and last letters

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious

explanation.surface: An abandoned burial chamber holds a strange relic.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a small fragment or bit of something.

clue.text: Following proper sex this compiler's crude

indicators.note: following says the next pieces come after the proper word

parts.note: prim means proper or prudish
it is a slang word for sex
the setter says I have, shortened to I've

explanation.surface: After prim lovemaking, the setter admits to being vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this compiler's' stands for the setter saying I have, written I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means basic and unsophisticated, so roughly made.

clue.text: Try hitching up motorway, backpacking initially

definitions.text: Try hitching up motorway, backpacking initially

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A backpacker hitch-hikes on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the thing: a hitchhiker sticks it out at the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchhikers signal for a lift by holding out this digit, so to try hitching is to use it.

clue.text: Hypocrisy from bank

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to tilt or slope, as an aircraft banks

explanation.walkthrough: 'from' joins the two senses; 'bank' is the verb to tilt, not a riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both sanctimonious insincerity and a slant or tilt.

clue.text: Shocking former sweetheart, guy accepts resistance

parts.note: ex means former
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, a standard crossword trick

indicators.note: accepts means taking the resistance inside

parts.note: a guy is a rope or cable holding something steady
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: An ex-girlfriend's chap takes up resistance, which is appalling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover, but it means the centre of the word sweet. A guy rope is a cable.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means extremely bad or abominable, so dreadful.
